evidence.reason: `claim_run_dir` creates `self.run_dir` under the record base and returns without fsyncing `base`. The later `durable_write` of the receipt can persist entries inside the run directory, but it cannot persist the new run directory's entry in its parent. On power loss, the host can remain held while the run directory and its prior SHA/trigger evidence are lost. If `base.mkdir` created the record base here, its parent entry is also unpersisted. This is an ordinary crash-consistency defect in existing durable recovery behavior, not a new requirement.
